questions.q: '___ umbrella' and '___ European country' — pick a or an for each.
questions.a: 'an umbrella' (vowel sound) and 'a European country' (yoo- consonant sound). A wrong answer 'a umbrella'/'an European' shows the student is matching letters, not sounds.

questions.q: 'I saw ___ elephant. ___ elephant was drinking water.'
questions.a: a, then The — first mention introduces with 'a'; second points back with 'the'. A wrong answer 'a' twice shows the student doesn't track shared knowledge across sentences.

questions.q: Fix: 'The honesty is the best policy.'
questions.a: 'Honesty is the best policy' — abstract/general nouns take no 'the' when meaning the whole idea. A wrong answer keeping 'the' shows over-specification.

questions.q: 'a' and 'an' introduce something new and ______; 'the' points at something specific that both people know.
Fill in the blank: 'a' and 'an' ______ something new and non-specific; 'the' points at something specific that both people know.
Fill in the blank: The ______ broke.' First mention = a (new to the story), every mention after = the (we know which one).
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student chooses a/an/the by the shared-knowledge test, picks a vs an by pronunciation not spelling, and explains first-mention-a versus second-mention-the.
